scoring_note: Demo-only: published case, possibly memorised and findable by retrieval. Slot 01 is scored with cases/_alt/01_guitarist_drd_synthetic/. See cases/manifest.json.
source_citation: Adapted from: Hasegawa T, Hosaka T, Harada R, Kawahata I, Hoshino K, Sugeno N, Kikuchi A, Aoki M. Case Report: Guitarist's cramp as the initial manifestation of dopa-responsive dystonia with a novel heterozygous GCH1 mutation. F1000Research 2021;10:361. doi:10.12688/f1000research.51433.1. License: CC BY 4.0. Videos: Hasegawa T (2021), Dryad, doi:10.5061/dryad.pzgmsbckd, CC0 1.0. Patient consent for publication of clinical details and videos was obtained by the original authors. Case text paraphrased and reorganized into this schema; investigations that would reveal the diagnosis are moved to the held-out reference. Fields the source does not report are marked as such and were not invented.

reference_diagnosis.name: Dopa-responsive dystonia, GCH1-related (autosomal dominant GTP cyclohydrolase 1 deficiency), adult-onset presentation as guitarist's cramp
reference_diagnosis.basis: Per Hasegawa et al. 2021: action-induced right upper limb dystonia beginning as guitarist's cramp and losing task specificity; normal MRI and DAT SPECT; low CSF HVA, 5-HIAA and total neopterin; marked and sustained improvement the day after starting levodopa 300 mg/day; novel heterozygous GCH1 variant c.542T>G (p.Val181Gly) predicted pathogenic by SIFT and PolyPhen-2.

acceptable_top5: Idiopathic task-specific focal dystonia / musician's dystonia
Other monogenic isolated dystonia (e.g. TOR1A, THAP1, GNAL)
Early-onset Parkinson disease presenting with limb dystonia (e.g. PRKN, PINK1)

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Onset after a sharp increase in practice, right-hand pick-holding difficulty, adult onset, prior specialist diagnosis
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Loss of task specificity with spread to everyday tasks; no response to an anticholinergic; levodopa trial never done — not excluded on clinical grounds alone

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: Early-onset Parkinson disease presenting with dystonia
competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Young-adult limb dystonia can precede parkinsonism in PRKN/PINK1
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: No parkinsonism after ten years; DAT SPECT normal (held out)
No family history reported; adult onset atypical for TOR1A; genetics identify GCH1 (held out)

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Must be considered in any dystonia under ~50
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Normal serum copper and ceruloplasmin, normal MRI, no hepatic or psychiatric features; slit lamp and urine copper not reported, so formally incomplete
No positive functional signs reported; consistent action-induced pattern over ten years

key_evidence_gaps.question: Has a levodopa trial ever been done?
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: A levodopa trial is recommended in young-onset dystonia regardless of phenotype; a dramatic response points to DRD

key_evidence_gaps.question: Presynaptic dopaminergic imaging (DAT SPECT)
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Normal in DRD; reduced in early-onset PD

key_evidence_gaps.question: CSF neurotransmitter metabolites and pterins
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Low HVA and neopterin support GTP cyclohydrolase 1 deficiency

key_evidence_gaps.question: Genetic testing (GCH1 and other dystonia/parkinsonism genes)
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Confirms the subtype and distinguishes from PRKN-PD and TOR1A/THAP1 dystonia

key_evidence_gaps.question: Detailed family history and examination/testing of relatives
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: GCH1-DRD is autosomal dominant with reduced penetrance; relatives may have mild or unrecognized symptoms

held_out_evidence.result: Marked improvement of the dystonia on the following day, sustained; well controlled without adverse effects at 6-month follow-up. Post-treatment video available (media/01_S2_post_levodopa.mov, source Video S2).
held_out_evidence.media_note: 8.6 s, no audio, face out of frame, different clothing (recorded on a later day). Right hand opens and closes a water-bottle cap repeatedly and smoothly, without the abrupt finger hyperextension seen in the agent-visible clip. For the demo reveal; not needed for scoring.

held_out_evidence.result: Normal radioligand binding in both caudate nuclei and putamina.
HVA 22.6 ng/mL (ref 41.6–178), 5-HIAA 9.1 ng/mL (ref 20.0–96.0), total neopterin 2.0 pmol/mL (ref 9.0–20.0): all decreased. Biopterin not reported.
Novel heterozygous GCH1 variant c.542T>G (p.Val181Gly) in exon 5, at a highly conserved residue in the C-terminal enzymatic core; SIFT and PolyPhen-2 predict pathogenic.
Not reported in the source publication.
Not reported in the source publication.

discriminating_investigations.discriminates_between: DRD (dramatic, sustained) vs. idiopathic focal dystonia (little or no response) vs. early PD (response with later fluctuations)

discriminating_investigations.investigation: Genetic testing including GCH1 (sequencing plus deletion/duplication analysis), TH, SPR, PRKN, PINK1, TOR1A, THAP1
discriminating_investigations.discriminates_between: Confirms DRD subtype; distinguishes from PRKN-PD and other monogenic dystonias; sequencing alone misses GCH1 exon deletions
Supports GTP cyclohydrolase 1 deficiency when genetics are negative or uncertain

cant_miss.condition: Dopa-responsive dystonia (GCH1 and other dopamine-synthesis disorders)
cant_miss.why_required: Treatable with low-dose levodopa; EFNS 2011 recommends a levodopa trial in early-onset dystonia without an alternative diagnosis
cant_miss.addressed_by: Supervised levodopa trial; GCH1 genetics with deletion/duplication analysis
cant_miss.status_in_record: open: no levodopa trial, no genetics

cant_miss.why_required: Treatable; must be considered in anyone under 50 with a new movement disorder
cant_miss.addressed_by: Slit lamp exam for Kayser-Fleischer rings and 24-hour urine copper
cant_miss.status_in_record: partly addressed: serum copper and ceruloplasmin normal (no estrogen exposure reported); slit lamp and urine copper not reported

cant_miss.why_required: Reversible if the drug is stopped
cant_miss.status_in_record: addressed: no regular medication before onset

red_flags_for_wrong_reasoning: Accepting the prior 'guitarist's cramp' label without addressing the loss of task specificity or the absence of a levodopa trial (anchoring on prior diagnosis)
Ruling out DRD because there is no diurnal variation or because onset was in adulthood (adult GCH1 cases often lack diurnal fluctuation)
Inventing diurnal fluctuation, sleep benefit, lower-limb involvement, or a positive family history — none are in the case record
Treating the normal MRI as evidence against DRD or for any specific diagnosis
Concluding Parkinson disease from levodopa responsiveness alone without DAT imaging
Declaring Wilson disease fully excluded on serum copper and ceruloplasmin alone
Labelling the presentation functional because the symptoms briefly remitted with a change of instrument, without positive functional signs
Recommending DBS, surgery, or medication as an instruction rather than a consideration for the treating physician
Stating any diagnosis as established rather than as a hypothesis for physician review
Citing literature that does not exist or that does not support the specific claim
expected_system_behavior: DRD should appear in the Top 5 with an explicit recommendation of a levodopa trial, despite the absence of diurnal variation, because the dystonia is young-onset, has lost task specificity, and never had a levodopa trial. The levodopa result and Video S2 are the demo's reveal.
